Prevention: Before sowing, complete mouldboard ploughing to expose resting pupae in the soil to heat and the sun.
May to avoid the second generation of the spotted bollworm.
Keep up sufficient fertilizer application to strengthen the plants, such as nitrogen (4-5 bags/acre).
Use trap crops such as bajra, maize, jawar and hibiscus.
Eradicate weeds such as kanghi buti, peeli buti, congress grass, puthkanda, itsit and tandla to destroy alternate plant hosts in or near the field.
Remove cotton stubbles immediately after the last cotton picking of the season to remove caterpillars and pupae.
Destroy crop residues at the end of the season (September) to remove overwintering pupae.
Monitoring: Monitor the pest mid-June when cotton is in the flowering stage.
Monitor during the early morning or evening, twice a week.
Observe the shoots, buds, squares, flowers, and bolls of cotton for the caterpillars.
They are brown, whilst the cotton bollworm is green/grey.
Symptoms include holes and rotting on bolls, shedding on squares and drying during the pre-flowering stage.
At 5 to 10 young caterpillars per 30 plants/field, consider direct action.
Install 2 to 5 light traps per acre.
Adult moths are 1.5 to 2.5 cm long.
Head, thorax and legs are pale apple-green and white beneath.
Forewings are bright apple-green with pale long streaks; the hind wings are pale apple-green tinged with pink.
Install 2 pheromone or kairomone traps, at 9-12 adult moths/trap/day, consider direct action.
